title: Scotch stitch pincushion
subtitle: A 9 cm square pincushion in alternating Scotch stitch blocks on 13-count canvas
excerpt: This pincushion uses alternating Scotch stitch blocks in two colours on 13-count canvas to produce a diagonal chequerboard pattern. Finished as a box-edge cushion and stuffed firmly with polyester filling, it stands about 3 cm deep.
sourceNotes: Stitch arrangement derived from Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), canvaswork stitches chapter. Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), scotch stitch entry.

glossaryTerms.definition: A cushion construction in which a strip of fabric joins the front and back panels to give the cushion a three-dimensional box shape with straight sides rather than a flat pillow edge.

heroPrompt: A small square needlepoint pincushion in dark teal and cream showing alternating Scotch stitch blocks, pins inserted, on a wooden sewing table, natural light.

content.text: This pincushion is worked on 13-count canvas in a two-colour alternating Scotch stitch layout. Each Scotch stitch block covers a 5 by 5 hole area and consists of five diagonal stitches. The alternating colour placement creates a diagonal chequerboard across the 45 by 45 hole design area. The finished size is 9 by 9 cm, stuffed and backed with felt.
What you need

items.label: Thread A: main (dark)
items.value: Persian wool. Suggested: DMC 930 / Anchor 1035 (dark antique blue). About 5 m

items.label: Thread B: contrast (light)
items.value: Persian wool. Suggested: DMC 712 / Anchor 926 (cream). About 5 m

items.label: Stuffing
items.value: Polyester toy filling or wool roving, about 30 g

items.label: Backing
items.value: Felt or plain cotton, 10 by 10 cm

items.label: Box strip
items.value: Plain cotton, 3 cm wide by 38 cm long, for the side gusset

content.text: Palette
Thread A: DMC 930 / Anchor 1035: dark antique blue
Thread B: DMC 712 / Anchor 926: cream
Stretching the canvas
Mount the canvas on a hoop or frame before starting. Scotch stitch pulls at an angle and the canvas will distort if worked in the hand.
Stitches used
Scotch stitch
only. Each block covers a 5 by 5 hole square in five diagonal stitches: over 1, 2, 3, 2, 1 threads.
Working method
Mark the canvas centre with two basting threads. Count 22 or 23 holes from centre to find the design boundary on each side, giving a 45 by 45 hole area.
Start from the top-left corner of the design area. Work the first Scotch stitch block in Thread A. Work the adjacent block in Thread B. Continue alternating across the row.
On the next row, start with Thread B where you used Thread A above, and vice versa. This produces the chequerboard layout.
Continue until the 45 by 45 area is complete. Secure thread ends by running the needle back under three or four stitches on the reverse. Do not knot the thread end where the stitch sits.
Block the canvas by dampening and pinning square to a board. Leave overnight.
Finishing
Trim the canvas margin to 1.5 cm. Cut the gusset strip and sew it around the needlepoint front, right sides facing, to form the
box-edge cushion
sides. Sew the felt backing to three sides of the box strip. Stuff firmly. Close the fourth side by hand.
What to try next
A three-colour Scotch stitch layout, where each block is one of three cycling colours, produces a more complex pattern on the same canvas count.
